main_text.p: ut ipsum tangerent, quotquot tenebantur flagellis. Marc.5.29. Hæmorrhu-fa sensit corpore se sanatam esse ex eo flagello. Luc.13.16. Hanc aute filiam Abra-hæ, quam vinxerat Satan ecce decem & octo annos, non oportuit a vinculo isto solui die Sabbathi?

De æstu Solis lædente corpora nostra, exemplum habemus in hac ipsa historia de Ionah, qui arefacta hedera, propter Solis æstum doloribus capitis laborauit. Aliud exemplum de puerulo Sunamitidis filio, quę Elisæus refuscitauit, exstat 2.Reg.4.18.19.

De intemperantia, quæ multorum morborum causa est, obseruent Studiosi di-ftū[?] memorabile Prouerb.23.29. Cuinam uæ? cui (inquam) uæ? cui rixæ? cui murmur? cui vulnera absque causa? cui rubor oculorum erit? 30. His qui immorantur circa vinum, euntibus ad disquirendum miftū[?]. 31. Ne igitur intuearis vinū quod rubrum fit, quod det in calice colorem suum, agitet se probè. 32. In fine velut serpens mordebit, & velut regulus dolore afficiet.
Etsi autem peccata fæpenumero cau-fæ[?] sunt

page.notes: Reading of the running text is clear apart from the marked words. "di-ftū" (line 4 of the paragraph) is probably "dictū" with a ct ligature printed as ft; I have kept the printed form and marked it. "miftū" is uncertain and kept as printed. "fæ" at the end is uncertain: it may be "sæ" or "fæ". The last line "fæ funt" is indented, so it is a continuation line, not a new paragraph. Hyphenated words are kept with their printed hyphens. Long s is written as s throughout. The small mark under the last line is not printed text and is left out.
